transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. A small amount of clean water left in the bottom under the filter after a cycle finishes is actually normal. This 'residual water' keeps the internal seals moist and prevents odours from rising up through the drain hose. If the water is just around the filter area (about a cup's worth) and smells clean, your dishwasher is likely draining perfectly. However, to be sure it isn't a partial blockage or an installation issue, please twist and lift out the flat filter at the bottom of the tub. Is there only a small amount of clear water in the sump underneath (normal), or is the water level significantly higher than the filter base?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

Thanks, I've taken the filter out. There's only a small amount of clear water in the sump under it, roughly a cupful, and none in the main tub. It's the same the next day, not rising. No error codes either.

That suggests it is normal. A small amount of clear water left in the sump (about a cupful) after the cycle finishes is by design; it keeps the internal seals moist and prevents odours from rising up through the drain hose. You don't need to do anything else.

candidates: Normal residual water in the sump (high)
Blocked filter or debris in the sump (medium)
Installation issue (kinked hose or blocked sink waste) (medium)
